result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.to_directed()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Convert the graph to a directed graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11412-L11481){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.to_directed() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Creates a new graph with the same nodes but directed edges. If the graph is already directed, returns a new copy. For undirected graphs, creates both directions (u->v and v->u) for each edge. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new directed Graph with the same nodes and bidirectional edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#0ca9ef25 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec undirected = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) directed = undirected.to_directed() directed.is_directed() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Each undirected edge becomes two directed edges, one for each direction: ::: {#24f034bf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} directed.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: This is useful for preparing an undirected network for directional analysis, such as comparing flow in each direction along a road: ::: {#4bc60862 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} roads = ec.Graph(directed=False) roads.add_node(label="A") roads.add_node(label="B") roads.add_node(label="C") roads.add_edge("A", "B", weight=5) roads.add_edge("B", "C", weight=3) traffic = roads.to_directed() traffic.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['A->B', 'B->A', 'B->C', 'C->B'] ``` ::: ::: It's also the standard way to prepare an undirected graph for algorithms that only operate on directed graphs, like cycle enumeration: ::: {#46918cee .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="X") g.add_node(label="Y") g.add_node(label="Z") g.add_edge("X", "Y") g.add_edge("Y", "Z") g_dir = g.to_directed() g_dir.get_cycles() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` [[1, 2], [3, 2]] ``` ::: :::
